text_blocks.snippet: Wilson's disease, a genetic disorder causing excessive copper accumulation in the body, has a broad differential diagnosis, encompassing various liver and neurological conditions. Key considerations include other causes of liver disease (like viral hepatitis, autoimmune hepatitis, and alcoholic liver disease) and neurological disorders (such as Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, and dystonia).

list.title: Acute and Chronic Hepatitis:
list.snippet: Viral hepatitis (A-E), autoimmune hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and other chronic liver diseases can mimic Wilson's disease's hepatic presentation.
